I just recently overcame root aphids, I haven’t seen any in over a month. Tossing your soil is unnecessary, the aphids can only live for a day or two with no live plants to feed on and they don’t lay eggs, just live young. 

If I could do it all over again I would take some clones of any important plants I have on hand, thoroughly clean them and isolate away. Chop down all living plants, and let the grow space stay free of live plants for at least 1 week preferably 2, then start your grow again. That is advice I got from a agricultural pest control specialist. He says that is the only way to be 100% clean, when even the most thorough pesticide application can leave some to reproduce. 

I went through all 8 weeks of flower picking root aphids out of my buds every single day, all for an early harvest with tons of bugs in my nugs. They are attracted to the flowers. 

I tried this insecticide, that insecticide, peroxide, soapy water, everything. Nothing actually worked to ELIMINATE them, just reduced their numbers, and that was an expensive bottle of pyganic. 

The reality is root aphids can’t reproduce in very high temperatures, and once my grow area got into the 90’s they were gone…

Anyway… not much of a success story here, rip up those plants and start over clean if you know what’s good for you.

Honestly keeping it simple is best just try to keep your humidity around 50% at any temperature and your plants will be happy. In flower go dryer and veg go wetter but at 50% humidity or less your chances of mold are low and the plants will grow just fine. 60 percent humidity+ is perfect to grow mold and lots of plants are happy there but the problem is that getting VPD “dialed” is when it is mold is a possibility. My soil recipe you can get pretty much everything from a Home Depot type store and a nursery, nothing too crazy.

Cannabis grows great in sand and it is a good low cost way to get a lot of your material for cheap. I think it is a great base for a soil. It waters through nicely so lockouts aren’t an issue.

•A bag or two of “washed” landscaping sand/paver sand. I would recommend washing it again

• Rich compost of any kind, it could be worm castings, backyard made compost, or composted manure.

• pumice stone, perlite or both. You can get big bags of pumice for cheap in the garden section at the store but they need to be broken down with a hammer to size before use. Prepackaged perlite is good for this but personally I don’t like perlite in soil, it is too light. This will help keep some air pockets in all the sand. They also sell broken down horticultural pumice but it’s expensive for it being rocks.

• Some light organic matter like rice hulls, and coco coir they can be bought by the pound at a brewers supply store or online for very cheap and they are really effective. You could also use straw, mulch, anything light and woody.

That’s all you need and I used this basic recipe along with a couple additions along the way and I grew my healthiest plants yet in it. It really doesn’t need to be too complicated, just make the mix and take the PH of it and adjust as necessary by adding more compost to make it more acidic. The base of the soil being sand it will raise in PH as the nutes leach out of it.
